thread:
maria: quick heads-up — saw reproducible divergence after quantizing magnet-13b to int4v2 when running long-prefill scenarios (~12k+ tokens). short repro and logs below. :eyes:

devon: what kind of divergence? output truncation or semantics drift?

maria: not semantic drift per-se. model starts emitting repeated fragments then drops mid-sentence around prefill boundary. seems tied to prefill length + shard tiling. non-deterministic whether it happens but high rate on canary. example run: 
```
$ ./tests/long_run.sh --model magnet-13b-int4v2 --tokens 15000 --prefill 10240 
INFO: prefill=10240 tiles=80 tile_size=128
KV_INDEX: writing 0..10239
READ_START: 10240
ERROR: kv_read_mismatch at pos=10241 expected_key=0x7f3a got=0x1c2b
TRACE: rope_phase_index= -1 0 127 128 129 ...
```

jon: hmm looks like an index roll-over at the tile boundary. could be RoPE wrapping + quantized memcpy alignment. did you try forcing PREFILL_TILE=128 vs 256?

maria: yeah. PREFILL_TILE=128 reduces frequency but doesn't eliminate on multi-shard runs. single-shard runs fine.

devon: can you dump the raw kv index arrays and a tiny token stream around the transition? npy preferred. also include shard id mapping.

maria: uploading dumps to s3: s3://redwood-ml-debug/maria/magnet-13b-int4v2/1768004321/ (prefill.npy, kv_indices.npy, meta.json). link has perms open to eng-ml.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered canary rollout magnet-13b-int4v2 -> hosts: gpu-dedicated-07..09 (3/5)

jon: try running with KVCACHE_DEBUG=1 and set ROTARY_BASE_OVERRIDE=10000 for one run to see if RoPE scaling is the culprit. also set REDWOOD_PREFILL_ALIGN=256 to detect misaligned memcopy.

maria: ran that. attaching short log snippet: 
```
KVCACHE_DEBUG: shard=1 read_offset=10240 read_len=2048 aligned_to=256
ROTARY_BASE=10000 effective_scale=0.99998
KVCACHE_CHECKSUM: expected=0x9a1f actual=0x9a1f OK
--- later ---
KVCACHE_CHECKSUM: expected=0x8b3c actual=0x2a1d MISMATCH pos=10241
```

devon: checksum failure after alignment step — points to memcopy/quant dequant boundary bug in multi-shard gather. maybe a rounding bug when computing absolute kv index across shards.

eva: is this blocking the canary? we should throttle if error rate >1% for production. canary metrics show 0.6% so far.

maria: I paused the wider rollout and bumped canary to 5 hosts for more coverage. job: https://console.redwood.ai/canaries/1768004321

jon: next steps I suggest: (1) reproduce with int8 (to rule out int4 packing), (2) enable bytewise memcopy sanity assert in runtime (cheap), (3) bisect the quant kernel changes from last week.

maria: started int8 run now. will also run a targeted bisect with the quant kernel commit range 0a1..0f2.

ops-bot: canary update: magnet-13b-int4v2 error_rate=0.4% -> 0.3% over last 10m :thumbsup:

devon: cool. if int8 is clean, it's likely our packing/unpacking path. otherwise check rotary param scaling code between gather and prefill.

maria: int8 run looks clean after 3k tokens. uploading new logs to s3. scheduling a 30m joint session tomorrow 10:30 PT to triage and bisect. anyone want on the call?

jon: I'll join. devon too. eva might attend for rollout decisions.

eva: i'll be there. can you add short agenda in the invite?

maria: invite sent. agenda: repro steps, quick bisect plan, temporary runtime guard (checksum assert), canary threshold adjustments.

devon: one more note — try reproducing with PREFILL_PADDING=1 (forces non-multiple-of-tile prefill) to see if we hit edge packing code paths.

maria: good idea. adding that to repro matrix. thanks all. :shipit:
